intro.title: Lines to remember
intro.description: From the films, and from the man himself.

lines.speaker: Amanda
lines.text: This is how you make dinosaurs?

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: No. This is how you play God.

lines.speaker: Erik
lines.text: I read both of your books. I liked the first one more. Before you were on the island. You liked dinosaurs back then.

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: Back then, they hadn't tried to eat me yet.

lines.speaker: Symposium Leader
lines.text: Now, does anyone have a question?
many people in the audience raise their hands

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: Fine. Does anyone have a question that does not relate to Jurassic Park?
most people lower their hand

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: Or the incident in San Diego, which I did not witness?
nearly everyone else lowers their hand

lines.speaker: Billy Brennan
lines.text: You have to believe me, this was a stupid decision, but I did it with the best intentions.

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: With the best intentions? Some of the worst things imaginable have been done with the best intentions. You know what, Billy? As far as I'm concerned, you're no better than the people that built this place.

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: I have a theory that there are two kinds of boys. There are those that want to be astronomers, and those that want to be astronauts. The astronomer, or the paleontologist, gets to study these amazing things from a place of complete safety.

lines.speaker: Erik
lines.text: But then you never get to go into space.

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: Exactly. That's the difference between imagining and seeing: to be able to touch them. And that's... that's all that Billy wanted.
a field of beautiful dinosaurs comes into view

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: Did you read Malcolm's book?
Erik nods

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: So?

lines.speaker: Erik
lines.text: I don't know. It was kinda preachy. And too much Chaos. Everything Chaos. It just seemed like the guy was high on himself.

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: That's two things we have in common.

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: It's OK. It's dead.
a T-Rex raises its head out of the carcass

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: Nobody move a muscle.
the T-Rex roars and the team runs off

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: Shit!

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: Why me?

lines.speaker: Paul Kirby
lines.text: He said we needed someone who'd been on the island before.

lines.speaker: Udesky
lines.text: Yes, but I did not tell you to kidnap somebody!

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: I have never been on this island.

lines.speaker: Paul Kirby
lines.text: Sure you have, you wrote that book.

lines.speaker: Billy Brennan
lines.text: That was Isla Nublar. This is Isla Sorna - Site B.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: Rawr! Rawr Rawr!

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: Actually, Charlie, those are herbivores. They really wouldn't be interested in fighting with each other, but these ones here are carnivores, and they really like fighting with each other. They'll use their teeth and claws to rip each other's throats out.

lines.speaker: Ellie Degler
lines.text: Alan, he's three. Let's wait till he's five.

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: Great, just great. We're in the worst place in the world and we're not even being paid.

lines.speaker: Erik
lines.text: Be careful with that. T-Rex. It scares some of the smaller ones away but attracts one really big one with the fin.

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: This is T-Rex pee?
Eric nods yes

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: How'd you get it?

lines.speaker: Erik
lines.text: You don't wanna know.

lines.speaker: Paul
lines.text: What are you doing? Those things are after us because of those!

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: Those things know we have the eggs. If I drop them in the river, they'll still be after us.

lines.speaker: Paul
lines.text: What if they catch us with them?

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: What if they catch us without them?

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: Erik, I have to tell you, I'm astonished that you've lasted eight weeks on this island.

lines.speaker: Erik
lines.text: ... Is that all it's been?

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: Oh my God.

lines.speaker: Amanda
lines.text: What is it?

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: It's a bird cage.

lines.speaker: Amanda
lines.text: For what?

lines.speaker: Billy Brennan
lines.text: I don't remember that one being on InGen's list.

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: It wasn't on their list. Which makes you wonder what else they were up to.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Are you saying you wouldn't want to get on Isla Sorna and study them if you had the chance?

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: No force on earth or heaven could get me on that island.

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: On this island there is no such thing as safe.

lines.speaker: Erik
lines.text: Wow. You have to thank her now. She sent the Navy and the Marines!

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: God bless you, Ellie.

lines.speaker: Billy Brennan
lines.text: I rescued your hat.

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: Well... that's the important thing.

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: We haven't landed yet.
last lines

lines.speaker: Erik
lines.text: Where do you think they're going?

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: I don't know. Maybe just looking for new nesting grounds. It's a whole new world for them.

lines.speaker: Amanda
lines.text: I dare 'em to nest in Enid, Oklahoma.

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: Reverse Darwinism - survival of the most idiotic.

lines.speaker: Paul Kirby
lines.text: What was that?

lines.speaker: Billy Brennan
lines.text: It's a Tyrannosaurus.

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: I don't think so. It sounds bigger.

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: Either way... you probably won't get off this island alive.

lines.speaker: Erik
lines.text: That lady you called.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Hmm?

lines.speaker: Erik
lines.text: Who is she? How do you that she can help us?

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: She was the one person I could always count on. I owe her a lot. Although I don't think I ever told her that.

lines.speaker: Erik
lines.text: You should.

lines.speaker: Ellie Degler
lines.text: So what were you doing?

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: Evolving.

lines.speaker: Billy Brennan
lines.text: Alan, I want to thank you for bringing me along.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Yeah, well, the bones will still be there when we get back. That's the great thing about bones; they never run away. The truth is, you got me into this, and I have no intention of being on my own with these people. Don't get too excited, Billy. Chances are we won't see a thing. Your turn to be nice. Wake me when we get there.

lines.speaker: Billy Brennan
lines.text: So, how'd it go?

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: Well, it's not too late to change your major, Billy.

lines.speaker: Billy Brennan
lines.text: Not good, huh?

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: Worse. We're gonna have to pack up in four weeks.

lines.speaker: Billy Brennan
lines.text: Three. I had to rent some equipment. Come here, I gotta show you something. You like computers, right?

lines.speaker: Dr. Grant
lines.text: I like the abacus, Billy.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: What are you doing?

lines.speaker: Billy Brennan
lines.text: I was photographing the nest.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Don't do that again.

lines.speaker: Billy Brennan
lines.text: Sorry.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ellie Sattler
lines.text: So, what are you thinking?

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: We're out of a job.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ian Malcolm
lines.text: Don't you mean extinct?
last lines

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Hammond, after careful consideration, I've decided, not to endorse your park.

lines.speaker: John Hammond
lines.text: So have I.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Come on. Come on.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: You got any kids?

lines.speaker: Dr. Ian Malcolm
lines.text: Me? Oh, hell yeah, three. I love kids. Anything at all can and does happen. Same with wives, for that matter.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: You're married?

lines.speaker: Dr. Ian Malcolm
lines.text: Occasionally. Yeah, I'm always on the lookout for a future ex-Mrs. Malcolm.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: T-Rex doesn't want to be fed. He wants to hunt. Can't just suppress 65 million years of gut instinct.

lines.speaker: Tim
lines.text: Well... we're back... in the car again.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Well, at least you're out of the tree.

lines.speaker: John Hammond
lines.text: ...And there's no doubt; our attractions will drive kids our of their minds!

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: And what are those?

lines.speaker: Dr. Ellie Sattler
lines.text: Small versions of adults, honey...

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: I guess that means the power's off.
Grant grabs the fence, pretending to be electrocuted and Lex and Tim scream

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: That's not funny.

lines.speaker: Tim
lines.text: That was great.

lines.speaker: Tim
lines.text: What do you call a blind dinosaur?

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: I don't know. What do you call a blind dinosaur?

lines.speaker: Tim
lines.text: A Do-you-think-he-saurus.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Ha ha. Good one.

lines.speaker: Tim
lines.text: What do you call a blind dinosaur's dog?

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: You got me.

lines.speaker: Tim
lines.text: A Do-you-think-he-saurus Rex.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Well, where does he think he's going?

lines.speaker: Dr. Ian Malcolm
lines.text: When you gotta go, you gotta go.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Their radio is out too. Gennarro said to stay put.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ian Malcolm
lines.text: The kids OK?

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: I didn't ask. Why wouldn't they be?

lines.speaker: Dr. Ian Malcolm
lines.text: Kids get scared.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: What's to be scared about? It's just a little hiccup in the power...

lines.speaker: Dr. Ian Malcolm
lines.text: I didn't say I was scared.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: I didn't say you were scared.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ian Malcolm
lines.text: I know.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Big Tim, the human piece of toast.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Mr. Hammond, the phones are working.

lines.speaker: John Hammond
lines.text: Are the children all right?

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: The children are fine. Call the mainland. Tell them to send the damn helicopters.
we hear the raptors smashing the windows

lines.speaker: Dr. Ellie Sattler
lines.text: It's gonna come through the glass!
Grant starts shooting at it. Hammond listens to the noises

lines.speaker: John Hammond
lines.text: GRANT!

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: They're moving in herds. They do move in herds.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Tim. Tim, can you tell me what they are?

lines.speaker: Tim
lines.text: They're, Gal... uh... uh, Galli... uh, Gallimimus.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: Are those... meat-eating... uh, meatasauruses?

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: The wheel uniform changes just like a flock of birds evading a predator.

lines.speaker: Tim
lines.text: They're, uh... they're flocking this way.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: What the hell do you think you're doing in here?
John pops open a bottle of champagne. The cork comes flying at Grant and he ducks

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Hey, we were saving that.

lines.speaker: John Hammond
lines.text: For today, I guarantee it.
They're feeding leafy branches to a docile Brachiosaurus

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: Can I touch it?

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Sure. Just think of it as... kind of a big cow.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Don't move! He can't see us if we don't move.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: What did I touch?

lines.speaker: Dr. Ian Malcolm
lines.text: Uh, you didn't touch anything. We stopped.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: What if the dinosaurs come back while we're all asleep?

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Hmm. I'll stay awake.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: All night?

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: All night.

lines.speaker: Tim
lines.text: I threw up.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Oh, well that's OK. Give me your hand.
Tim refuses to move from the car

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Tim, I won't tell anyone you threw up, just... just give me your hand.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: OK, it's just the two Raptors, right?
to Ellie

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: You're sure the third one's contained?

lines.speaker: Dr. Ellie Sattler
lines.text: Yes, unless they figure out how to open doors.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: He left us! He left us!

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: But that's *not* what *I'm* gonna do.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: What species is this?

lines.speaker: Henry Wu
lines.text: Uh, it's a velociraptor.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: You bred raptors?

lines.speaker: Dr. Ian Malcolm
lines.text: Hey, hey, hey, hey!

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Ian, freeze!

lines.speaker: Dr. Ian Malcolm
lines.text: Get the kids!
the T-rex sees the flare, roars at Malcolm, and runs after him

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Get rid of the flare!

lines.speaker: Dr. Ian Malcolm
lines.text: Get the kids!

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Get rid of the flare!

lines.speaker: Dr. Ian Malcolm
lines.text: She's, uh... tenacious.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: You have no idea.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: It's just like climbing down from a treehouse. Did your Dad ever build you a treehouse?

lines.speaker: Tim
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: No, dammit!

lines.speaker: Volunteer #1
lines.text: This new program's incredible. A few more years development and we won't even have to dig anymore.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Where's the fun in that?

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: Go away!

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: It's OK. It's OK. It's a Brachiosaur.

lines.speaker: Tim
lines.text: It's a veggiesaurus Lex! Veggiesaurus!

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: Veggie!

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: What are you and Ellie gonna do now if you don't have to pick up dinosaur bones anymore?

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: I don't know. I guess... I guess we'll just have to evolve too.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Uh... it's... it's a dinosaur!

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: What kind of park is this?

lines.speaker: John Hammond
lines.text: It's right up your alley.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: Sh. Sh. Don't let the monsters come over here.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: They're not monsters, Lex. They're just animals. And these are herbivores.

lines.speaker: Tim
lines.text: That means they only eat vegetables, but for you I think they'd make an exception.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: I hate the other kind.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: They just do what they do.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Ellie, this one was always my favorite when I was a kid. And now I've seen one, its the most beautiful thing I ever saw.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: I want to go now.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Look how it eats.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: Please!

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: I bet you'll never look at birds the same way again.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: I hate computers.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ellie Sattler
lines.text: The feeling's mutual.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: I hate trees!

lines.speaker: Tim
lines.text: It looks like it has a cold.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Yeah, maybe.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Keep absolutely still. Its vision is based on movement.

lines.speaker: John Hammond
lines.text: Well, we clocked the T-Rex at 32 mph

lines.speaker: Dr. Ellie Sattler
lines.text: T-Rex... , you said you've got a T-Rex?

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Say again

lines.speaker: John Hammond
lines.text: We have a T-Rex

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Hey!

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Lex, Lex you're choking me! Grab the wire! Grab the wire!
Lex grabs a loose wire of the electric fence just as the T-Rex pushes the car with Tim inside over the edge just missing Grant and Lex by inches

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: Timmy!

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Tim!
the T-Rex tries to push the car with Tim inside over an embankment

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Look at the pubic bone, turned backward.

lines.speaker: Dr. Alan Grant
lines.text: Dinosaurs eat man. Woman inherits the earth.

quotes.text: Of all the characters I've played, I think I have more in common with that guy than with Reilly: Ace of Spies (1983) referring to Carl Fitzgerald in Death in Brunswick (1990). Who Weekly (NZ) 8/23/93.

quotes.context: Referring to The Simpsons (1989) — EW, 7/23/93
quotes.text: I'm playing a cat burglar. I've made it. This is the high point of my career. I'm really chuffed
If all I did was acting, I'd go out of my mind.
The pathetic thing about actors is they don't feel valid unless they're acting.

quotes.context: 2012, on Dead Calm (1989
quotes.text: ) Well, that was fantastically good fun, actually, although quite a lot of the time we were seasick and cold and wet and stuff like that. It was a very interesting film to do, as there were only three characters, you know, but it works very well, and it built quite a few careers. For [director] Phillip Noyce, it launched him into big action films, and there's this Australian actress called Nicole Kidman in it who you might've heard of...

quotes.context: 2014, on socializing with Michael Williams and Warren Clarke during the making of Enigma (1982)
quotes.text: My liver is still recovering.

quotes.context: on changing his name from Nigel to Sam, aged ten
quotes.text: I saved myself a lifetime of pain.

quotes.context: Tell us a secret.
quotes.text: I was christened Nigel. It set me back for years.

quotes.context: Which living person do you most admire, and why?
quotes.text: My brother, Michael. He is an academic and has devoted his life to scholarship; my life seems trivial by comparison. Bastard.

quotes.context: What did you want to be when you were growing up?
quotes.text: A soldier like my father. I would have been useless.

quotes.context: Which words or phrases do you most overuse?
quotes.text: I'm sorry to say, the word is fuck.

quotes.context: What keeps you awake at night?
quotes.text: Worrying about insomnia.

quotes.context: What do you most dislike about your appearance?
quotes.text: Pretty much all of it. But these weird fat bits on my hips - yuck!

quotes.context: What song would you like played at your funeral?
quotes.text: I Will Remember You, by Sarah McLachlan. That'll choke the bastards up if nothing else will.

quotes.context: What is the trait you most deplore in yourself?
quotes.text: Sloth. No, wait, greed. No, gluttony.

quotes.context: What has been your biggest disappointment?
quotes.text: My complete ineptitude at sport.

quotes.context: What is the worst job you've done?
quotes.text: Everyone says it's the Fifa film [United Passions], but I had a marvellous time.

quotes.context: Who would play you in the film of your life?
quotes.text: Tilda Swinton.

quotes.context: What makes you unhappy?
quotes.text: Solitude. I crave company.

quotes.context: What is your guiltiest pleasure?
quotes.text: Come Dine With Me. Everything you need to know about the British in one tidy hour.

quotes.context: What is the worst thing anyone's said to you?
quotes.text: Did we sleep together? Really? Are you quite sure?

quotes.context: on working with Meryl Streep on Plenty (1985) and A Cry in the Dark (1988)
quotes.text: By the time we did the second I was very comfortable with her. She scared the shit out of me in the first one. I was too young and too bedazzled by her. I was daunted. And I think on day one we had a sex scene. I wonder how many actors have done sex scenes with Meryl Streep. Probably just a handful.

quotes.context: on Priscilla: Queen of the Desert
quotes.text: The only regret I do have is that I did turn down Priscilla. It's probably indiscreet to say, but I'll say it anyway - Terence Stamp ended up playing the part. It would've been fun to play with my mate Hugo [Weaving] and Guy [Pearce], of course. I made a mistake there, because it wasn't about being in drag, which I'd be happy to do - I wear a dress all the time anyway.
Where we're going, we won't need eyes to see.
Hell is just a word. The reality is much worse.
I would have liked to have seen Montana.
Me and this fat kid, we ran, we ate, and read books, and it was the best.
Pretty majestical, aye?
